rationale: The Airflow OTEL integration must honour the OpenTelemetry precedence rule that signal-specific env vars override the generic one; omitting this case leaves a silent regression risk in the tracer/metrics setup code

rule: Use the sentinel pattern from AirflowConfigParser to distinguish a user-explicitly-set Airflow config value from a default, rather than comparing against OTel env vars directly
trigger: code that reads an Airflow OTEL/observability config key and then checks whether an OTel env var is also set, without using a sentinel fallback
rationale: There is no way to know if the user set the Airflow config versus accepted the default; the AirflowConfigParser sentinel pattern (see airflow/_shared/configuration/parser.py) is the established Airflow mechanism to detect this and is required to emit correct deprecation warnings

rule: Do not assert a hard-coded total plugin count in plugin-manager tests; assert the specific deduplication or presence behaviour instead
trigger: assert len(plugins) == <integer literal> in plugin manager tests
rationale: The total count changes whenever any provider adds or removes a plugin, making the assertion brittle and unrelated to the behaviour under test (deduplication of entrypoint provider plugins)

evidence.excerpt: Brittle: changes whenever any provider adds/removes a plugin, doesn't verify deduplication

rule: Assert serialization truncation output using the exported TRUNCATE_PREFIX and TRUNCATE_SUFFIX constants rather than a loose substring check
trigger: assert '...' in result or assert 'Truncated' in result used to verify serialize_template_field truncation output
rationale: A loose 'in' check passes even when the format regresses (missing suffix, wrong prefix, extra content); the helpers module exports TRUNCATE_PREFIX and TRUNCATE_SUFFIX for exact regression assertions

evidence.excerpt: Assert exact output using TRUNCATE_PREFIX + TRUNCATE_SUFFIX to make the regression test precise

rule: Wrap config-dependent tests that call resolve_state_backend() (or similar config-reading functions) in a conf_vars context manager to prevent non-deterministic failures from global config state
trigger: call to resolve_state_backend() or other Airflow config-reading functions in a test without a conf_vars({...}) context manager
rationale: Without conf_vars isolation a test passes by accident against config.yml defaults and fails non-deterministically when a prior test modifies global config without cleanup

evidence.excerpt: Depends on global config state; if previous test sets state.backend and forgets cleanup, fails non-deterministically

rule: Use `with create_session() as session:` and pass the session explicitly; never call create_session().__enter__() without a matching __exit__()
trigger: create_session().__enter__() used without a corresponding __exit__() call or without a with-statement
rationale: create_session is a generator-based context manager in utils/session.py; calling __enter__() alone leaves the generator suspended at its yield so the commit() and session.close() in the finally block only run on garbage collection, silently relying on internal commits and scoped-session semantics

evidence.excerpt: Leaves create_session generator suspended; commit/session.close only run on GC

rule: Use 'override' (not 'overwrite') when describing Helm values files passed via -f or --set, consistent with the chart's mergeOverwrite helper naming
trigger: the word 'overwrite' used in Helm chart documentation to describe values file or --set flag precedence
rationale: 'override' is already used throughout the chart Helm docs and aligns with the mergeOverwrite/mustMergeOverwrite helper names; 'overwrite' is a different concept and is not used elsewhere in the chart

rule: In Helm pod-template-file fallback chains, use `or` rather than `| default` so that the global fallback value (e.g. .Values.containerLifecycleHooks) is included, consistent with every other fallback chain in the chart
trigger: | default used in pod-template-file.kubernetes-helm-yaml for a value that should fall back through workers.kubernetes.<key> -> workers.<key> -> global <key>
rationale: | default stops at two levels and misses the global .Values.containerLifecycleHooks fallback that the rest of the chart provides via `or`; this silently drops the global default for kerberos init container settings

rule: Use `hasKey` to distinguish an unset new Helm key from an explicitly empty value; do not use `| default` to fall back to a deprecated key, because `| default` treats an empty map as falsy and silently ignores an intentional empty override
trigger: | default .Values.<deprecated-key> used in Helm templates to fall back from a new workers.kubernetes.<key> to an old workers.<key>
rationale: | default on a map treats {} (explicitly set to empty) as falsy and falls back to the deprecated key, preventing users from intentionally clearing annotations/lifecycle-hooks while still having the legacy key set; hasKey correctly distinguishes 'not provided' from 'set to empty'

evidence.excerpt: Explicitly empty workers.kubernetes.podAnnotations: {} falls back to deprecated workers.podAnnotations; use hasKey to distinguish unset from empty

rule: A new feature belongs in the Helm chart only if more than ~80% of production users will need it; apply the Pareto principle alongside the existing 'required to run Airflow' criterion
trigger: addition of a new Helm chart component or value that is optional or serves a minority use-case
rationale: The chart CONTRIBUTING guide explicitly states the Pareto principle: components used by fewer than ~80% of users belong in kustomize overlays, not the core chart, to keep the chart lean

evidence.excerpt: Pareto principle applies: >80% must need and use this function for productive use
